newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas shares start year on record note, end up.
newsitem.headline: Caracas shares start year on record note, end up.

text.p: Caracas stocks began the year as they ended 1996 -- on a record note -- to reach a new high but in relatively quiet trading, traders said.
The market's leading 19-share index finished up 2.20 percent to close at 6,837.05 points.
A total 55.7 million shares were exchanged, worth 3.66 billion bolivars ($7.71 million), with nearly two-thirds of the total cross-trades.
Among traded issues on the stock exchange, 26 rose, eight fell and five closed flat.
"There was surprisingly strong demand for Electricidad de Caracas, CANTV and Mavesa, but little volume," trader Eduardo Blanco of Cavelba said.
He predicted a similar trend over the next week.
Total trade was boosted by large cross trades in paints and packaging company Corimon B shares and investment company Fondo de Valores Inmobiliarios.
The Caracas bolsa had a record 1996, scoring the biggest increases on the International Finance Corporation (IFC) composite index of emerging market equities, with gains of nearly 115 percent.
